detail.body: # PR Draft: Qwen3.5 Transformers 5 DynamicCache Status: prepared for human review; the clean branch is pushed to the personal fork, but no upstream PR has been created. The branch is rebased onto the latest canonical `main` (`5b550b0c3dad8c7bb7aab834a3fe195f8cdfc517`). PR #7471 is still open, so its eventual merge should be checked for overlap before submission. ### What does this PR do? Title: `[model] fix: support Transformers 5 Qwen3.5 dynamic cache` Transformers 5 stores Qwen3.5 gated-delta-net convolution and recurrent state inside layer-scoped `DynamicCache` entries and exposes update methods instead of the legacy top-level arrays. The verl training monkey patch still used the old fields, so a cached forward failed before a GRPO update. Cached multi-token continuations also need the previous convolution context and recurrent state. This patch supports both legacy and Transformers 5 cache APIs, preserves state through chunked continuation, and adds a CPU regression test for prefill, multi-token continuation, single-token decode, and chunk/token equivalence. ### Duplicate-work check - Canonical repository: `https://github.com/verl-project/verl` - Related open PR: [#7471](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7471) resolves current Transformers 5 Qwen3.5 kernel/block-type names in the same module, but does not address the DynamicCache state API or continuation flow. - Related work searched: #6212, #8190, #8192, #7653, #7749, and the vLLM- Ascend Qwen4Exp work. None is an exact DynamicCache duplicate. - Publication must be coordinated with #7471. Preferred form is a cache-only follow-up rebased onto its final merge SHA; the integration merge commit is retained only for conflict and runtime validation. ### Test Environment: Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.10.0, Transformers 5.5.4, `TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0`. CPU tests ran in `verlpr_env`. The real GRPO smoke used an A3 container with CANN 9.0.0, `torch_npu 2.10.0.post4`, vLLM 0.22.1, vLLM-Ascend 0.22.1rc1, and Qwen3.5-2B. Rebased cache-only PR branch (`4b37dc93`, based on `5b550b0c3dad8c7bb7aab834a3fe195f8cdfc517`): ```text python -m pytest -q tests/models/test_qwen35_dynamic_cache_on_cpu.py \ tests/models/test_fused_kernels_ulysses_sp_on_cpu.py 27 passed ``` Fresh rebase logs: - `autopr/evidence/qwen35-v1-a3/rebase-fae3256c/pytest-qwen35-dynamic-cache.log` (`1 passed, 14 warnings`) - `autopr/evidence/qwen35-v1-a3/rebase-fae3256c/pytest-fused-kernels-ulysses-cpu.log` (`26 passed, 14 warnings`) - `autopr/evidence/qwen35-v1-a3/rebase-fae3256c/pre-commit-changed-files.log` (all hooks passed) The combined `27 passed` result above is retained as historical evidence from the pre-rebase checkout; the two fresh logs are the acceptance evidence for the current HEAD. Additional compatibility evidence: - Focused DynamicCache/kernel-resolution tests: `13 passed, 1 skipped` on Transformers 5.5.3, 5.5.4, and 5.12.1. Fresh overlay logs for 5.5.3 and 5.12.1 are `autopr/evidence/qwen35-v1-a3/followup-transformers-553-cpu-20261014.log` and `autopr/evidence/qwen35-v1-a3/followup-transformers-512-cpu-20261014.log`. - Current-main plus #7471 integration: fused-kernel suite `26 passed` and focused suite `13 passed, 1 skipped`. - Changed-files and all-files pre-commit passed on the prepared checkouts. - Real A3 V1 GRPO two-step run completed with non-constant reward range `0..1`, step-1 advantage range `+-0.7071`, step-1 gradient norm `0.0125406`, and weight synchronization `5.2276 s` / `4.9003 s`. Fresh cache-only PR GRPO one-step smoke on A3 also completed rollout, reward, actor update, and vLLM weight synchronization: reward range `0..1`, advantage range `-0.7071..+0.7071`, non-zero actor gradient norm `0.0086453`, weight synchronization `5.1273 s`, and step time `61.49 s`. This is a path and update smoke, not a convergence claim. The base reproducer fails before the actor update with: ```text AttributeError: 'DynamicCache' object has no attribute 'conv_states' ``` The PR regression passes with `1 passed, 14 warnings`. A fresh PR GRPO run reached vLLM rollout and four reward calls, then stopped in the unrelated generic nested-tensor actor indexer: ```text RuntimeError: split_with_sizes expects split_sizes to sum exactly to 28 (input tensor's size at dimension 1), but got split_sizes=[4, 4, 4, 4] ``` No DynamicCache traceback occurred in that run. The complete status is recorded in `comparison-swanlab-metrics-20261015.json`. GRPO logs and metrics: `autopr/evidence/qwen35-v1-a3/`. ### Experiment figures The figures below are generated from the metrics uploaded to SwanLab. They are diagnostic smoke-test plots, not claims of model convergence or benchmark improvement. [DynamicCache regression outcome] [Cache-only PR GRPO success smoke] [GRPO timing] For completeness, the following plot is from the previously validated integration candidate that also contains #7471 kernel-resolution changes. It is not cache-only PR evidence and is shown only to document the conflict-resolution and runtime-validation experiment. The whole training curves are coming soon. SwanLab runs: - Comparison record: https://swanlab.cn/@lzc12138/qwen35_dynamic_cache/runs/j5l30vlp - Cache-only PR success smoke: https://swanlab.cn/@lzc12138/qwen35_dynamic_cache/runs/1wgahoxs ### API and Usage Example No public API or configuration change. Existing legacy cache objects remain supported. ### Design & Code Changes - Resolve cache state from either legacy arrays or Transformers 5 layer entries. - Use Transformers 5 cache update methods when available, with legacy fallback. - Pass cached convolution/recurrent state into chunk continuation and retain only newly generated outputs. - Request and store final recurrent state whenever a cache is active. ### Checklist Before Submitting - [x] Search for similar PRs. The related #7471 search and scope distinction are recorded above. - [x] PR title follows the required format: `[model] fix: ...`. - [x] Contribution and AI-assistance rules read. - [x] Duplicate-work research recorded. - [x] Focused tests, fused-kernel tests, pre-commit, and GRPO evidence recorded. - [x] No user-facing documentation change needed; this is an internal compatibility fix with a regression test. - [x] SwanLab comparison and cache-only PR smoke metrics uploaded; figures are generated locally from the same JSON metrics. - [x] Human submitter reviews every changed line and confirms cache API/test assertions. - [x] Check whether the still-open #7471 changes the target module before submission. - [ ] Final target CI image checks are rerun by the human submitter after any #7471 coordination. - [ ] Human sign-off/attribution is added according to `AGENTS.md`. - [x] Personal fork branch was pushed after authenticated owner/repository verification. - [ ] `ci-request` channel notification and upstream CI are handled by the human submitter after publication. ### AI Disclosure Implementation and validation were AI-assisted. A human submitter must review and defend every changed line before publication. ### Publication State The rebased branch was pushed to `LZC-BELIEVER/verl:fix/qwen35-dynamic-cache`. The compare API verified `ahead_by=1`, `behind_by=0`, base `5b550b0c3dad8c7bb7aab834a3fe195f8cdfc517`, head `4b37dc931ba7bde524fe379140d4af98cad1d1dc`, and exactly the two files listed above. Review link: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/compare/main...LZC-BELIEVER:fix/qwen35-dynamic-cache No upstream PR was created, no comments/reviews were posted, and no CI was triggered. SwanLab uploads were previously verified with `swanlab verify`; the fresh rebase checks are recorded in the handoff.

+
+"""Regression tests for the Transformers 5 Qwen3.5 cache API."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+pytest.importorskip("transformers.models.qwen3_5")
+
+from transformers.cache_utils import DynamicCache
+from transformers.models.qwen3_5.configuration_qwen3_5 import Qwen3_5TextConfig
+from transformers.models.qwen3_5.modeling_qwen3_5 import Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet
+
+from verl.models.transformers.qwen3_5 import (
+    _cache_has_previous_state,
+    qwen3_5_gated_delta_net_forward,
+)
+
+
+class _LinearAttentionLayerCache:
+    def __init__(self, indexed: bool):
+        self.conv_states = {0: None} if indexed else None
+        self.recurrent_states = {0: None} if indexed else None
+        self.has_previous_state = {0: False} if indexed else False
+
+
+class _DynamicCacheDouble:
+    """Minimal cache double matching tensor and Transformers 5.16.1 shapes."""
+
+    def __init__(self, indexed: bool):
+        self.layers = [_LinearAttentionLayerCache(indexed)]
+        self.indexed = indexed
+
+    def has_previous_state(self, layer_idx: int, state_idx: int | None = None) -> bool:
+        previous_state = self.layers[layer_idx].has_previous_state
+        if self.indexed:
+            return all(previous_state.values()) if state_idx is None else previous_state[state_idx]
+        return previous_state
+
+    def update_conv_state(self, conv_states: torch.Tensor, layer_idx: int, state_idx: int = 0, **kwargs):
+        del kwargs
+        layer = self.layers[layer_idx]
+        if self.indexed:
+            layer.conv_states[state_idx] = conv_states
+            layer.has_previous_state[state_idx] = True
+        else:
+            layer.conv_states = conv_states
+            layer.has_previous_state = True
+        return conv_states
+
+    def update_recurrent_state(self, recurrent_states: torch.Tensor, layer_idx: int, state_idx: int = 0, **kwargs):
+        del kwargs
+        layer = self.layers[layer_idx]
+        if self.indexed:
+            layer.recurrent_states[state_idx] = recurrent_states
+            layer.has_previous_state[state_idx] = True
+        else:
+            layer.recurrent_states = recurrent_states
+            layer.has_previous_state = True
+        return recurrent_states
+
+
+def test_qwen35_dynamic_cache_selects_state_zero_for_indexed_state_flags():
+    cache = _DynamicCacheDouble(indexed=True)
+    cache.layers[0].has_previous_state = {0: True, 1: False}
+
+    assert _cache_has_previous_state(cache, layer_idx=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "cache_kind",
+    ["transformers", "tensor-valued", "state-indexed"],
+    ids=["transformers", "tensor-valued", "state-indexed"],
+)
+def test_qwen35_gated_delta_net_accepts_both_dynamic_cache_state_shapes(cache_kind):
+    config = Qwen3_5TextConfig(
+        vocab_size=128,
+        hidden_size=16,
+        intermediate_size=32,
+        num_hidden_layers=1,
+        num_attention_heads=2,
+        num_key_value_heads=1,
+        head_dim=8,
+        linear_key_head_dim=4,
+        linear_value_head_dim=4,
+        linear_num_key_heads=1,
+        linear_num_value_heads=2,
+        linear_conv_kernel_dim=4,
+        layer_types=["linear_attention"],
+        dtype=torch.float32,
+    )
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    layer = Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet(config, layer_idx=0).eval()
+    reference_layer = Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet(config, layer_idx=0).eval()
+    sequential_layer = Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet(config, layer_idx=0).eval()
+    reference_layer.load_state_dict(layer.state_dict())
+    sequential_layer.load_state_dict(layer.state_dict())
+    cache = (
+        DynamicCache(config=config)
+        if cache_kind == "transformers"
+        else _DynamicCacheDouble(indexed=cache_kind == "state-indexed")
+    )
+    reference_cache = DynamicCache(config=config)
+    sequential_cache = (
+        DynamicCache(config=config)
+        if cache_kind == "transformers"
+        else _DynamicCacheDouble(indexed=cache_kind == "state-indexed")
+    )
+    hidden_states = torch.randn(1, 4, config.hidden_size)
+    continuation_states = torch.randn(1, 2, config.hidden_size)
+    decode_states = torch.randn(1, 1, config.hidden_size)
+
+    output = qwen3_5_gated_delta_net_forward(layer, hidden_states, cache_params=cache)
+    reference_output = reference_layer(hidden_states, cache_params=reference_cache)
+    continuation_output = qwen3_5_gated_delta_net_forward(layer, continuation_states, cache_params=cache)
+    decode_output = qwen3_5_gated_delta_net_forward(layer, decode_states, cache_params=cache)
+
+    qwen3_5_gated_delta_net_forward(sequential_layer, hidden_states, cache_params=sequential_cache)
+    sequential_continuation = torch.cat(
+        [
+            qwen3_5_gated_delta_net_forward(
+                sequential_layer, continuation_states[:, :1], cache_params=sequential_cache
+            ),
+            qwen3_5_gated_delta_net_forward(
+                sequential_layer, continuation_states[:, 1:], cache_params=sequential_cache
+            ),
+        ],
+        dim=1,
+    )
+    sequential_decode = qwen3_5_gated_delta_net_forward(sequential_layer, decode_states, cache_params=sequential_cache)
+
+    assert output.shape == hidden_states.shape
+    assert torch.isfinite(output).all()
+    assert continuation_output.shape == continuation_states.shape
+    assert torch.isfinite(continuation_output).all()
+    assert decode_output.shape == decode_states.shape
+    assert torch.isfinite(decode_output).all()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(output, reference_output)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(continuation_output, sequential_continuation, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(decode_output, sequential_decode, rtol=1e-4, atol=1e-5)

+def _cache_has_previous_state(cache_params, layer_idx: int) -> bool:
+    """Support both the legacy cache flags and Transformers 5 layer caches."""
+    if cache_params is None:
+        return False
+    has_previous_state = getattr(cache_params, "has_previous_state", False)
+    if callable(has_previous_state):
+        try:
+            return bool(has_previous_state(layer_idx, state_idx=0))
+        except TypeError:
+            try:
+                return bool(has_previous_state(layer_idx))
+            except TypeError:
+                return bool(has_previous_state())
+    if isinstance(has_previous_state, Mapping):
+        return bool(has_previous_state[0])
+    return bool(has_previous_state)
+
+
+def _cache_state_at_zero(states):
+    return states[0] if isinstance(states, Mapping) else states
+
+
+def _cache_layer_states(cache_params, layer_idx: int):
+    layers = getattr(cache_params, "layers", None)
+    if layers is not None:
+        layer = layers[layer_idx]
+        return _cache_state_at_zero(layer.conv_states), _cache_state_at_zero(layer.recurrent_states)
+    return cache_params.conv_states[layer_idx], cache_params.recurrent_states[layer_idx]
+
+
+def _qwen35_kernel(self, module, attribute_name: str, module_name: str):
+    kernel = getattr(self, attribute_name, _MISSING)
+    if kernel is _MISSING:
+        kernel = getattr(module, module_name)
+    return kernel
+
+
+def _cache_update_conv_state(cache_params, conv_state: torch.Tensor, layer_idx: int) -> None:
+    update = getattr(cache_params, "update_conv_state", None)
+    if callable(update):
+        update(conv_state, layer_idx)
+    else:
+        cache_params.conv_states[layer_idx] = conv_state
+
+
+def _cache_update_recurrent_state(cache_params, recurrent_state: torch.Tensor, layer_idx: int) -> None:
+    update = getattr(cache_params, "update_recurrent_state", None)
+    if callable(update):
+        update(recurrent_state, layer_idx)
+    else:
+        cache_params.recurrent_states[layer_idx] = recurrent_state
+

**🩺 Stability & Availability** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**

**Read state-indexed layer caches as tensors.**

With Transformers 5.16.1, `layer.conv_states` and `layer.recurrent_states` are dictionaries keyed by state index. This helper returns the dictionaries rather than state `0`. A cached multi-token continuation then fails at `torch.cat`, and one-token decode passes a dictionary to `causal_conv1d_update`. The unpinned `verl-core` dependency permits this version. Select state `0` for state-indexed caches while preserving the tensor-valued path, and extend the regression test to cover both shapes.
